header_summary:
DropKick, a novel Bitcoin protocol designed to assist users who delay transitioning to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), uses blockchain to make hidden commitments that can be later revealed to protect against quantum threats. The protocol embeds a commitment in the blockchain, which, when revealed with a PQ-signature from a post-quantum public key, allows the spending of legacy coins in a secure wallet. This mechanism leverages the blockchain's trustless timestamping to protect early knowledge of a secret, enhancing security without the need for centralized indexes, thus simplifying implementation compared to similar protocols like Tadge Dryja's Lifeboat. For more information on DropKick's operational details, please visit [conduition.io/bitcoin/dropkick](https://conduition.io/bitcoin/dropkick). [Source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/ruufSzDPIml1W5hF-m_IJLeBzuhqey6CGe7-zT1WwY4vlhVj_5NJTSalz43T4ZlZgXs3sDesW61FaU_asfj39Ri1QgSXtz7-OekEt6bbTvo=@proton.me/T/#u#m984f22f8a646298cfe2ad2461916f5ff1043c858)

Michael, known as fanquake, has released a new set of test binaries for Bitcoin, incorporating an updated version of glibc and available for various architectures. These binaries support both debug and standard versions and include guix hashes for security verification. This update marks a significant development in the Bitcoin software ecosystem, demonstrating the community's commitment to enhancing performance and stability through regular updates and active feedback. For details and downloads, visit the [GitHub page](https://github.com/fanquake/bitcoin/releases/tag/static_bitcoind_db73d1623957). [Source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/391ad3ce-2352-42d8-9d15-e011e187cb0fn@googlegroups.com/T/#m5ddf81712d352faf60e6e636157f336e53c5b434)

Debates surrounding the adoption of the P2TRv2 protocol highlight concerns over possible mempool congestion and increased blockchain storage needs due to hash-based signatures in a post-quantum world. Discussions also emphasize the strategic necessity for businesses to plan for potential fee rate spikes and increased block sizes, which could impact network operations significantly. These considerations underscore the need for future-proofing blockchain technology against quantum threats by potentially adjusting block size to accommodate new cryptographic practices. For a deeper exploration of these strategic implications, refer to [this detailed discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/pqc-output-type-discussion/2749/8).
